## Verdict: no agent-facing context, and `crimes` flags it explicitly

The scan surfaces it as **`crime_00011` — Missing Agent Context** (`missing_agent_context`, universal pack), severity `medium`, confidence `0.90`, `agent_risk` 0.47:

```
no AGENTS.md found at repo root
no CLAUDE.md found at repo root
no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present
no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present
package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands
```

One caveat on reading the JSON: it's anchored to `assets/cjs_shims.js`, but it's a **repo-level** finding — the file field is just an anchor, not the offending file. Don't go looking for the problem in that shim.

## Why this matters for your first PR

This repo ships a build tool (`tsup` / `tsup-node`) with 52 files, a real plugin surface, and no written conventions. The rest of the scan shows precisely what an agent will get wrong without them:

- **Load-bearing files with no warning label.** `src/utils.ts` (fan-in 18, 425 lines), `src/plugin.ts` (fan-in 10), `src/log.ts` (fan-in 9), `src/index.ts` (fan-out 17, 460 lines). An agent asked to "clean up utils" will restructure a module 18 files depend on, and nothing in the repo tells it not to.
- **The test suite won't catch the mistake.** 12 tests have **zero** `expect`/`assert` calls (`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`, `test/tsconfig.test.ts`, `test/experimental-dts.test.ts`) and ~14 more use only weak matchers. Green CI here means "it ran," not "it works." An agent reads green and ships.
- **Deliberate idioms look like bugs.** `fs.*Sync` throughout `src/fs.ts`, `src/utils.ts`, `src/api-extractor.ts` is normal for a build CLI, but `sync_io_in_hotpath` fires on all of it. Same for `Date.now()` in the timing paths (`src/tsc.ts`, `src/rollup.ts`, `src/esbuild/index.ts`) — that's duration logging, not domain non-determinism. With no AGENTS.md, every agent re-litigates these from scratch, and some will "fix" them.
- **Options shapes are implicit.** `runEsbuild` reads **38 distinct properties** off an untyped `options` bag; `getRollupConfig` reads 10; `main` reads 8. Nothing documents which fields are required or who owns them.

The compound effect: an agent lands a confident, plausible-looking change to a high-fan-in module, the assertion-free tests pass, and the break shows up downstream in someone's build.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

The detector looks for `AGENTS.md` at the repo root (or `CLAUDE.md`, or a `SKILL.md` under `.claude/skills/` / `.agents/skills/`). Any one of them clears it — but write the content, not just the file, or you've cleared a detector without buying anything. This skeleton is grounded in what the scan actually found:

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

## What this is
`tsup` — a zero-config TS/JS bundler wrapping esbuild (JS output),
rollup + api-extractor (`.d.ts` output), and swc (target lowering).
Binaries: `tsup`, `tsup-node`.

## Commands
- Install:   pnpm install
- Build:     pnpm build
- Test:      pnpm test          # full suite is slow — it runs real builds
- Single:    pnpm test <file>   # e.g. pnpm test test/index.test.ts
- Typecheck: pnpm typecheck
- Lint:      pnpm lint

<!-- Replace the above with the actual scripts in package.json before committing. -->

## Layout
- src/index.ts          entry: normalizeOptions -> build -> buildAll/startWatcher
- src/esbuild/          JS output path (esbuild plugins: svelte, swc, postcss)
- src/rollup.ts,
  src/api-extractor.ts,
  src/tsc.ts            .d.ts output path (runs in a child process)
- src/plugin.ts         plugin container + lifecycle hooks
- src/utils.ts,
  src/log.ts            shared helpers — see "load-bearing" below
- test/utils.ts         test harness (`run`); every test file imports it

## Load-bearing — read importers before editing
| File | Fan-in | Note |
|---|---|---|
| src/utils.ts   | 18 | shared helpers; additive changes only |
| src/plugin.ts  | 10 | plugin lifecycle contract |
| src/log.ts     |  9 | logger shape is depended on widely |
| test/utils.ts  |  9 | changing `run`/`output` breaks the whole suite |

Prefer adding a new function over changing an existing signature in these.

## Conventions (these are intentional — do not "fix" them)
- **Sync fs is fine.** This is a build CLI, not a server. `fs.*Sync` in
  `src/fs.ts`, `src/utils.ts`, `src/api-extractor.ts` is deliberate.
- **`Date.now()` in build paths is timing instrumentation**, not domain
  logic. Don't inject a clock abstraction for it.
- **Options bags are the public API.** `Options` in `src/options.ts` is
  user-facing; `runEsbuild` reads ~38 fields off it. Adding a field means
  updating the type, the CLI flag, and the docs together.

## Testing
- Tests shell out to real builds via `run()` in `test/utils.ts`. They are
  slow and I/O-heavy. Run a single file while iterating.
- **A green suite is weaker than it looks**: several existing tests assert
  nothing (`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`,
  `test/shims.test.ts`) or only check that output is non-empty. Do not
  treat "tests pass" as proof a change is safe.
- New tests must assert on `outFiles` / file contents, not just that the
  build completed.

## Safety
- Never edit `dist/` or `assets/*.js` by hand — generated/vendored.
- Don't change the `.d.ts` pipeline (rollup + api-extractor + tsc) and the
  esbuild pipeline in the same PR; they fail independently.
- Don't add runtime deps without discussion — this ships as a build tool.
```

Re-run `crimes scan --format json` after adding it; `crime_00011` should drop out and the summary goes to 91 findings (7 high / 39 medium / 45 low — `missing_agent_context` was a medium).

Two things I'd flag as your call: I haven't verified the actual `package.json` scripts or that `src/options.ts` is where `Options` lives — the scan JSON doesn't include either, so the Commands section and that one path reference need a quick check against the repo before this lands. Everything else in the skeleton is drawn directly from findings above.
